reason: The chlorine counts are consistent with the arrow labels, but the submitted molecular structures are not. B and D have incorrect carbon-skeleton connectivity; D also has the wrong number of unpaired electrons. C has the chlorine and radical at the wrong relative positions and incorrect bond orders. The Lean theorems only compute equalities between candidate-defined structures after embedding unsupported AFM site assignments and bespoke result-producing transformations. The target file compiles using only standard Lean axioms, but this does not establish the source chemistry, and the default project build additionally fails because IChO2026Problems/All.lean is missing.

coverage.evidence: The theorem proves the candidate's structureB, whose makeOutput definition removes both fusion bonds and requires a single 14-membered cycle. Inspection of the source AFM panel and the corresponding molecular structure in the primary scientific source shows B (C14Cl3) has a fused six-/ten-membered skeleton with one radical, not the submitted monocycle. See [Nature primary article, Extended Data Fig. 12 d–f](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06741-x/figures/16).

Although the C14Cl formula and one-radical count are correct, structureC places Cl at c3 and the radical at opposite site c10 and assigns several formal triple bonds. The molecular structure corresponding to source panel C has the radical on the carbon adjacent to the chlorine-bearing carbon and a different cumulene-like bond pattern. See [Nature primary article, Fig. 4 h(i)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06741-x). The claimed c_to_cyclo14_consistency instead forces an alternating polyyne endpoint by definition.

The source arrow supports C14Cl5, but the submitted D is a fully monocyclic 14-carbon ring with one radical. The exact AFM panel corresponds to an opened bis(chloroethynyl)-substituted fused-ring framework bearing three radical sites, as shown in [Nature primary article, Extended Data Fig. 12 g–i](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06741-x/figures/16). Thus connectivity, bond orders, and radical multiplicity are wrong.

unsupported_assumptions: All of B, C, and D are assumed to have both anthracene fusion bonds absent and every perimeter bond present; this is false for B and D.

The site-loss lists lossAtoD, extraLossDtoB, lossBtoC, and lossCtoC14 are asserted as pixel transcriptions, but the arrow labels establish only loss counts, and the resulting site assignments do not reproduce the depicted intermediates.

retroBergmanLeft, retroBergmanRight, pairAdjacent, and closeC14Polyyne are candidate-defined graph rewrites with result-shaped bond updates, not proved consequences of the printed retro-Bergman relation or a trusted general law.
The shared radicalAt10 field assumes exactly the same single radical site for B, C, and D; D actually requires three unpaired electrons, while C's radical is adjacent to its chlorine-bearing carbon.

The alternating-polyyne C14 endpoint is asserted as an independent check, although it is constructed directly by closeC14Polyyne and conflicts with the cumulene-like C14 assignment supported by the source AFM and primary scientific reference.
